schema.description: An edge with commentary: a fact that joins facets, with or without words, and the person's notes are edges of kind `about`. Named note.annotation until card 147 and record.note until card 191, whose v2 (card 104) made the note an edge; v1 here is record.note v2 under its new name, so every record.note value is a record.edge value unchanged. `from` and `to` are each a list of facet ids and `kind` says what the join means; a note about some facets is an edge of kind `about` with no `from`, the kind every record.note v1 value has. The facets it names are never changed by it; the edge is appended beside them, carries its own provenance (the person, typed, or the conversation that took it down, or a model's reading), and is retracted or edited on its own. Its fact time is the moment it was asserted (v2 of note.annotation, 2026-10-13): the one time nothing else holds, since each facet it names carries its own fact time, and anam-time is the ingest, not the writing. Which version of each named facet was current when the edge landed is read from the ledger at that watermark, not stored here; `pins` may name the exact version where that matters. A value carries words, ends, or both: `text` alone is an account that names nothing yet (card 157), a later version of the same id can name them. `about` is record.note v1's name of `to`, accepted so that a value written to it is a record.edge value unchanged; a value carries one of the two, and a later version drops `about` once every writer sends `to`. Links are read back from the record, never written into the facets an edge names: a facet's read shows the live edges touching it as a derived part beside its payload.

source_time.description: How the fact time, `at`, was read (card 198): value is the wall clock as said, zone the zone it was said in (an IANA name when the writer knows one, else the offset again), offset the offset from UTC it had then, and basis who decided the zone (source when the person's own client or browser names it, configuration when the writer's setting does). The fact time is `at` read at offset. Every value admitted before this version has none and was read in Australia/Sydney.

value.description: The fact time as the source supplied it, as text and never rewritten: a date, a wall clock, an RFC 3339 string, or an epoch as its digits.

zone.description: The zone value is read in, and nothing else: an IANA name when one is known, UTC for a value that is UTC, else a fixed offset +HH:MM or -HH:MM. The gate refuses a name that is no zone.

offset.description: The offset from UTC value had at that moment in zone, +HH:MM or -HH:MM, which names one instant even in an hour the zone repeats. A writer that cannot tell it refuses rather than guess.

basis.description: Who decided the zone. source: the source supplied it with the value, or the value is UTC by the source's own definition. configuration: a setting a person made for this source names it. assumption: the importer or writer chose it, with nothing behind it but its own default or the Definition's zone, and logged that it did.

id.description: The edge's own id, chosen once by whoever writes it, and kept for every later version. In a records file the convention is note:<first 8 of the first facet id>:<n>, n counting the person's notes that start there from 1, so a second note is a second fact and not an edit of the first. A conversation writer derives it from the moment and the words, conversation:<16 hex of their sha256>, so the same words said once are one note however often they are sent. A model's reading (card 158) derives it from the note version it read and the fact it wrote.

at.description: The moment the edge was asserted, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM in Australia/Sydney, or at the offset source_time names: for a note, when it was written. This is the fact time; the facets the edge names are reached through `from` and `to`, each at its own fact time.

kind.description: What the join means, from a closed list; absent means `about`, which every record.note v1 value is. `about`: the person's words about the facets in `to`, no `from`, `text` required in practice. `interpreted_from` (card 158): the draft facts in `from` were a model's reading of the note versions in `to`, the versions pinned in `pins`, the model's reasoning in `text`. A new kind is a new version of this Definition, added when it has a writer.

from.description: The facet ids on the edge's from side, as the inspector shows them, one or more, or absent. What the side means is the kind's to say. A facet id is stable across the facet's versions, so the edge follows each facet through supersession; Anam does not check that an id is live when the edge is admitted.

to.description: The facet ids on the edge's to side: for a note, the facets it is about, one or more, or absent when it names none yet. record.note v1 named this field `about`; a value carries one of the two names, not both.

about.description: record.note v1's name of `to`, accepted so that a value written to it is a record.edge value unchanged. A writer sends `to`; a value with both is refused; a later version drops this field.

pins.description: The exact version of a named facet, where it matters: the facet id to the content hash of the version the edge was asserted against, as sha256:<hex>. For card 158's reading of a note version. A facet id here is one the edge names in `from` or `to`; nothing is pinned unless said.

text.description: The words, verbatim, as the person typed or said them; for a model's reading, its reasoning. Absent on an edge that is only a join.
examples: During a large work meeting, presenting.
